en: The Sūtra of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark, translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Tang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavat, having perfectly accomplished all Tathāgatas...

Established by the adamantine right gnosis, he wears a precious crown of empowerment that is manifold, extraordinary, and transcends the three realms. Possessing sovereign mastery and unimpededness in Mahāyoga, he has attained profound and wondrous wisdom and realized the Dharma of equality. His meritorious deeds are all fully perfected; according to the minds of sentient beings, he brings them all to complete satisfaction. Equal throughout the three periods of time, he is eternally unmoving and indestructible; his three karmas are as firm as adamant, and his body is a universal radiance.

He dwells within the palace of the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven in the Desire Realm; that royal palace is adorned with various exquisite features, all fashioned from great mani-jewels. Silken canopies, banners, and streamers reflect one another in a multitude of colors; pearl necklaces and jeweled bells chime as they are stirred by the wind. It is a place where all Tathāgatas constantly travel and tread, and which they all together praise as being foremost in auspiciousness.
There were eight million bodhisattva-mahāsattvas surrounding him before and behind, making offerings and paying him respect.
The Buddha preached the Dharma for them—good in the beginning, middle, and end; its meaning profound and far-reaching, its words skillful and elegant; pure, unadulterated, and perfectly complete.
Their names were:
Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Dharmacakrapravartin Bodhisattva, and Sarvamārapramardin Bodhisattva.
With such Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas as their leaders, the World-Honored One,
at that time amidst the great assembly, expounded for the sake of the Bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark of the Innately Pure Self-Nature of All Dharmas.
That is to say:
"The stage of purity in craving is the bodhisattva stage;
the stage of purity in views is the bodhisattva stage."
The stage of profound attachment to purity is the bodhisattva stage;
the stage of delighting in purity is the bodhisattva stage;
the stage of the treasury of purity is the bodhisattva stage.
The stage of adorned purity is the bodhisattva stage;
the stage of radiant purity is the bodhisattva stage;
the stage of bodily purity is the bodhisattva stage.
The stage of purity of speech is the bodhisattva stage;
the stage of purity of mind is the bodhisattva stage;
the stage of purity of form is the bodhisattva stage.
The stage of purity of sound is the bodhisattva stage;
the stage of purity of fragrance is the bodhisattva stage;
the stage of purity of taste is the bodhisattva stage.
The state of purity of contact is the stage of the bodhisattva.
Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure.
"The intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure; this is the purity of the Prajñāpāramitā.
At that time, having spoken this Dharma-gate, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: "Vajrapāṇi!"

If there is anyone who hears this Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark of the Innately Pure Self-Nature of All Phenomena, and it but once passes through their ears, all their affliction-obstructions, karma-obstructions, and dharma-obstructions, as well as their most grievous transgressions, will be spontaneously extinguished; they shall not be born in the evil realms until they attain Bodhi.

If there is another person who, throughout each day, can receive, uphold, recite, contemplate, and practice this, they will immediately, in this very body, attain the Vajra Samādhi of the Equality of All Dharmas;
for sixteen subsequent lifetimes, they shall attain the joy of sovereign play within all dharma-gates, and ultimately shall obtain the vajra-body of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas.
At that time, the Tathāgata spoke this mantra: “Haṃ (long-drawn out).

Then the World-Honored One, by means of the universal radiance-mark of all Tathāgatas, expounded for the sake of the bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark of Perfect Enlightenment, which is the quiescent nature of all Buddhas.
That is to say:
"The attainment of perfect enlightenment through the equality of the vajra, because the solid nature of great bodhi is like a vajra;
the attainment of perfect enlightenment through the equality of meaning, because great bodhi is of a single meaning."
One attains perfect enlightenment through the equality of phenomena, because the intrinsic nature of great bodhi is pure;
one attains perfect enlightenment through the equality of all things, because great bodhi is free from all conceptual discrimination.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished expounding this Dharma-gate, he further addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: “Vajrapāṇi!

If there should be anyone who hears this Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Reality of Perfect Enlightenment through the Fourfold Nature of Quiescence, and who receives, upholds, recites, contemplates, and practices it, you should know that such a person shall immediately transcend all evil realms and swiftly realize Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
At that time, the Tathāgata further spoke this mantra:

"Oṃ (prolonged). Then the World-Honored One, manifesting the form of Śākyamuni—the one who can subdue those sentient beings difficult to subdue among all Tathāgatas—expounded for the sake of the bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark of the Equality of All Dharmas.
That is to say:
"The nature of greed is free from conceptual proliferation;
the nature of hatred is free from conceptual proliferation."
Ignorance has the nature of being free from conceptual proliferation. Why?
Because all phenomena have the nature of being free from conceptual proliferation.
“The non-conceptual nature of all phenomena is itself the non-conceptual nature of the perfection of wisdom.
When the World-Honored One had finished teaching this Dharma-gate, he further addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: “Vajrapāṇi!”

If there is anyone who hears this Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark of the Equality of All Dharmas, and receives, upholds, recites, contemplates, and practices it, even if that person were to kill all sentient beings within the three realms, they would ultimately never fall into the evil destinies because of this.
Why is this? Because they have already received the discipline of taming the mind.
It should be known that such a person will swiftly attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, the Tathāgata further spoke this mantra:

"Haṃ (long-drawn-out call). Then the World-Honored One, by means of the mark of the self-nature purity of all Tathāgatas, expounded for the sake of the bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark of the Wisdom-Seal of Avalokiteśvara, which is the equality of all dharmas.
That is to say:
"The nature of greed in all worlds is pure; the nature of hatred in all worlds is pure.
Because the nature of greed and the nature of hatred in all worlds are pure, the nature of defilement in all worlds is pure; the nature of transgression in all worlds is pure."
Because the nature of defilement in all worlds is pure and the nature of sin is pure, the dharma-nature of all worldly phenomena and the nature of sentient beings are pure;
because the dharma-nature of all worldly phenomena and the nature of sentient beings are pure, the wisdom-nature of all worlds is pure;
and because the wisdom-nature of all worlds is pure, this is the purity of the *prajñāpāramitā*.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished expounding this Dharma-gate, he further addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: “Vajrapāṇi!

If there is anyone who hears this Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Reality of the Wisdom-Seal of Avalokiteśvara on the Equality of All Dharmas, and who receives, upholds, recites, and practices it with right mindfulness, such a person, though amidst the five desires and sensory dusts, will not be defiled by the faults of greed and desire. Just as a lotus flower, though in the mud, is not adhered to by the mud, such a person shall even swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
At that time, the Tathāgata further spoke this mantra:

“Kili (short *u*-sound). Then the World-Honored One, manifesting the aspect of all Tathāgatas as the lords of the triple world, expounded for the sake of the bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark, the Treasury of Wisdom Manifesting the Empowerment of All Buddhas.
That is to say:
"The gift of consecration, because it causes all to attain the sovereignty of the triple world;
the gift of wealth and treasures, because it causes all to have their wishes fulfilled."
"The gift of the pure Dharma, because it causes all beings to attain the true nature of all phenomena;
the gift of food and drink, because it causes the bodies and minds of all beings to obtain peace and happiness.
At that time, the Tathāgata further spoke this mantra:

“Tāṃ hūḥ. At that time, the World-Honored One again, by means of the secret treasury of the sign of the eternally abiding wisdom-seal of all Tathāgatas, expounded for the sake of all bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the profound reality-mark of the Prajñāpāramitā, the Vajra Wisdom-Seal of all Buddhas.
That is to say:
"The Vajra Body Seal held by all Buddhas, because of attaining the true essence of all Tathāgatas;
the Vajra Speech Seal held by all Buddhas, because of attaining mastery over all Dharma-gates;"
This is the Vajra Mind Seal held by all Buddhas, because it brings about the perfection of all samādhis;
it is the Vajra Wisdom Seal held by all Buddhas, because it causes one to attain the supreme body, speech, and mind as vajra.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished expounding this Dharma-gate, he further addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: “Vajrapāṇi!

If there be anyone who hears this Dharma-gate of the profound reality of the *prajñāpāramitā*—the Seal of the Adamantine Wisdom of All Buddhas—and receives, maintains, recites, and correctly contemplates it with right mindfulness, you should know that such a person shall achieve the supreme adamantine seal. They will attain perfection in all-encompassing wisdom and all manifold activities; their nature of body, speech, and mind will become like adamant, until they finally realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, the Tathāgata further spoke this mantra: "Āḥ.

Then the World-Honored One, by means of the mark of all Tathāgatas being eternally free from conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), expounded for the sake of the bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark, titled "The Chapter on the Turning Wheel of Syllables."
That is to say:
"All phenomena are empty because they lack intrinsic nature;
all phenomena are signless because they are free from all signs."
All dharmas are wishless, because they are free from all wishes;
all dharmas are pure by nature, because the *prajñāpāramitā* is pure.
At that time, the Tathāgata further spoke this mantra:

"Ā-u-ko (with the final syllable pronounced short). Then the World-Honored One, by means of the sign of all Tathāgatas entering the vast wheel-turning, expounded for the sake of the bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark of Entering the Vast Wheel-Turning.
That is to say:
"By entering the equality of the vajra, one attains entry into the wheel-turning of all Tathāgatas;
by entering the equality of meaning, one attains entry into the wheel-turning of all bodhisattvas."
"By entering the equality of phenomena, one attains entry into the wheel-turning of the sublime Dharma;
by entering the equality of all things, one attains entry into the wheel-turning of all.
At that time, the Tathāgata further spoke this mantra:

“Lam-chang-hu. At that time, the World-Honored One again, by means of the signs of the great skillful means of all Tathāgatas, expounded for the sake of the bodhisattvas the foremost, most extensive Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark of Making Offerings to All Buddhas.
That is to say:
"To give rise to the bodhicitta is itself the great skillful means of making vast offerings to all Buddhas;
to rescue and protect sentient beings is itself the great skillful means of making vast offerings to all Buddhas."
"To uphold the True Dharma is itself the great skillful means for making extensive offerings to all Buddhas.
At that time, having spoken this Dharma-gate, the World-Honored One further addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: "Vajrapāṇi!"

If there are those who hear this foremost and most extensive Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark for making offerings to all Buddhas, whether they write it themselves or instruct others to write it; whether they personally uphold it or instruct others to uphold it; whether they personally recite it or instruct others to recite it; whether they personally contemplate it or instruct others to contemplate it; or whether they personally make offerings to it or instruct others to make offerings to it.
"Whatever one does in accordance with this shall constitute a great and skillful means for making extensive offerings to all Buddhas.
At that time, the Tathāgata further spoke this mantra:

"Oṃ (long drawn out). Then the World-Honored One, again assuming the aspect of the Tathāgatas who are capable of subduing, expounded for the sake of the Bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark, the Secret Treasury of Wisdom, which is able to subdue and gather in all sentient beings.
That is to say:
"The equality of all sentient beings is the equality of anger;
the nature of the subduing of all sentient beings is the nature of the subduing of anger."
The true dharma-nature of all sentient beings is the true dharma-nature of anger;
the vajra-nature of all sentient beings is the vajra-nature of anger. Why is this?
"Because the nature of the subduing of all sentient beings is itself bodhi.
At that time, the Tathāgata further spoke a mantra, saying:

"Ho-cang-hu. Then the World-Honored One, abiding in the mark of equality common to all Tathāgatas, expounded for the sake of all Bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark of the Most Supreme Equality of All Dharmas.
That is to say:
"Because all dharmas are equal in nature, the perfection of wisdom is equal in nature;
because all dharmas are of the nature of the ultimate truth, the perfection of wisdom is of the nature of the ultimate truth."
Because all dharmas have the nature of dharma-nature, the *prajñāpāramitā* has the nature of dharma-nature;
because all dharmas have the nature of karmic function, the *prajñāpāramitā* has the nature of karmic function.
At that time, the Tathāgata further spoke this mantra:

“Kṣi-li-chang-hu. Then the World-Honored One, manifesting the aspect of being the refuge for all sentient beings through the power of all Tathāgatas, expounded for the sake of the Bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Nature of the Refuge of All Sentient Beings.
That is to say:
"All sentient beings are the Tathāgatagarbha, because the essential nature of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva pervades them;
all sentient beings are the Vajragarbha, because they are sprinkled by the water of the Vajragarbha."
All sentient beings are the treasury of the True Dharma, for they are of the nature described by the true words [of the Buddha];
all sentient beings are the treasury of wondrous karma, for they are impelled and enacted by skillful and wondrous karma.
At that time, the Tathāgata further spoke this mantra:

“Tiri (long vowel) hūḥ. Then the World-Honored One, by means of the ultimate, exhaustive characteristic of all Tathāgatas—which is immeasurable, boundless, and reaches the furthest limit—expounded for the sake of the bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark of Equality, which is immeasurable, boundless, and reaches the furthest limit of all dharmas.
That is to say:
"Because the Prajñāpāramitā is immeasurable, all Buddhas are also immeasurable;
because the Prajñāpāramitā is boundless, all Buddhas are also boundless."
Because the Prajñāpāramitā is of a single nature, all dharmas are also of a single nature;
because the Prajñāpāramitā is ultimately exhausted, all dharmas are also ultimately exhausted.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished expounding this Dharma-gate, he further addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: “Vajrapāṇi!

If there is anyone who hears this Dharma-gate of the *Prajñāpāramitā* of the ultimate reality of infinite, boundless, and final exhaustion, and who upholds, recites, and correctly contemplates it with right mindfulness, all the obstructions and burdens of such a person shall be completely extinguished without remainder; they will swiftly reach Bodhi and attain the Tathāgata’s vajra-body, achieving mastery.”
At that time, the Tathāgata further spoke this mantra: "Piao-chang-hu.

Then the World-Honored One, by means of the universal radiance of the secret dharmatā of all Tathāgatas free from conceptual proliferation, expounded for the sake of the bodhisattvas the Dharma-gate of the Great Bliss Vajra Amogha Unobstructed Definitive Entry into Dharmatā, the Supreme First Reality of Prajñāpāramitā, which is without beginning, middle, or end.
That is to say:
"Because all bodhisattvas are able to extensively perform services and offerings, they attain the most supreme great bliss;
because they attain the most supreme great bliss, they attain the unsurpassed great bodhi of all Buddhas."
Because they have attained the unsurpassed great bodhi of all Buddhas, they are able to subdue all demonic armies;
because they have subdued all demonic armies, they attain sovereignty over the triple world;
because they possess sovereignty over the triple world, they are able to universally benefit all sentient beings, bestowing upon them ultimate and supreme peace and happiness.
Why is this? The verse says:
"There are those of supreme wisdom who always remain within the cycle of birth and death."
Extensively delivering all sentient beings, yet not entering nirvāṇa;
the Prajñāpāramitā is the ultimate wisdom of skillful means,
capable of accomplishing pure karma and universally purifying all realms of existence.
Furthermore, by means of subduing greed and the like within all worlds,
even up to the Peak of Existence (*bhavāgra*), he remains pure and free from conflict or violence.
Abiding in the world of birth and death, the worldly dharmas cannot defile him.
Like a lotus of wondrous color, unstained by dust or grime;
The person of great desire who is utterly pure, the person who bestows great peace and happiness,
Masters over the triple world, performing steadfast benefit.
At that time, after the World-Honored One had spoken this Dharma-gate, he again addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: “Vajrapāṇi!

If there is anyone who hears this Dharma-gate of the Great Bliss Vajra Nature, the Reality-mark Prajñāpāramitā, and every morning throughout each day, either listens to it or recites it without interruption, you should know that all their karmic obstacles will naturally be extinguished, and their minds will always be harmonious and tranquil, attaining supreme bliss.”

In this very lifetime, one shall immediately achieve the realization of the Vajra-Amogha-Unobstructed-Entry-into-Dharma, and further, one shall achieve the adamantine, secret, and solid body of all Tathāgatas.
At that time, the Tathāgata further spoke this mantra:

"Svāhā! (drawn out with a long vowel). Then, after the World-Honored One had expounded the aforementioned Dharma-gates for the Bodhisattvas, he addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: "Vajrapāṇi!..."

This sūtra of mine is difficult to hear; if there are those who hear it, even as little as a single word, you should know that such persons have in the past already made offerings to various Buddhas and have planted roots of goodness in the presence of those Buddhas.

How much more so for those who fully hear, read, and recite it; you should know that such persons have certainly already made offerings to, paid homage to, revered, and praised eighty billion nayutas of buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River.
Wherever this sutra is located, that place shall be as if it possessed a stupa of all Buddhas.

Furthermore, if there is anyone who cherishes and values this sutra, constantly following, protecting, and never parting from it, such a person should receive the respect and offerings of the entire world;
such a person shall attain the supernormal power of recollecting past lives and be able to know the events of immeasurable kalpas in the past.
They shall not be disturbed by any Māra Pāpīyān; the Four Great Kings and all other devas will constantly follow and protect them;
they will be perpetually sustained by all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and they will be reborn in the pure lands of the ten directions according to their vows.

Vajrapāṇi! I have now briefly explained the merits of this Dharma-gate of the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark in this way; were it to be explained in detail, they would not be exhausted even at the end of an eon.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, Vajrapāṇi and the other bodhisattvas, as well as the entire assembly—including devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—all rejoiced greatly, and they faithfully accepted and practiced it.
The Sūtra on the Prajñāpāramitā of the True Mark (Bhūtanimitta)
